history.period: 1961 (construction year per myadhyatm.com; peopleplaces.in says 'supposedly built in 1961' - verify)
history.summary: Best-supported referent for the generic CSV row 'Shiva Temple | Dimapur': the Swayambhu Shiva temple at Singrijan village, Dimapur district - the most documented Shiva temple of the Dimapur area (myadhyatm.com, astroved.com, peopleplaces.in all describe it). Per myadhyatm.com, the temple was constructed in 1961 by local villagers around a Swayambhu (naturally formed) Shiva lingam, and its origin legend belongs to the Rangapahar Reserve Forest: a villager sharpening his knife on a stone saw liquid oozing from it, then dreamed three times that the stone was Lord Shiva commanding a temple be built there (a fourth dream carried a warning), after which the temple was raised in the forest. Astroved.com describes a simple North-Indian-style complex with a golden-yellow shikhara, bells at the sanctum entrance, a trishul and snake idol behind the lingam on its circular platform, and a bronze Nandi; astroved's stated travel distances (railway station 44 km, airport 164 km) look like generic template figures and are NOT used here - verify distances locally. Maha Shivratri is the major festival. Coordinates are an area-level pin for the Rangapahar/Singrijan village belt (the geocoder carries no Singrijan entry), NOT the exact shrine - verify the shrine's precise location on the ground. Media is empty: no image verifiably depicting this temple was found after genuine searching.

town_description: Singrijan is a village in Dimapur district, Nagaland, south-west of Dimapur city near the Rangapahar Reserve Forest - the setting of the temple's origin legend. Dimapur, the district's main city, is Nagaland's largest commercial hub with the Kachari Ruins, the Kalibari, and the ISKCON temple; its airport and railway station link it to Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi.
